claude.sample_unit: frequently asked questions (plus 10 conditions of patient education materials)

links.outcome: Reading grade level of LLM responses to patient FAQs and default education materials
links.effect: FAQ responses averaged grade 15.3 (ChatGPT), 15.7 (Gemini), 14.6 (Copilot); default education materials 15.1, 14.8, 14.6 grade level, far above the recommended seventh grade.
links.quote: However, the default reading level of these responses was substantially higher than what is recommended by the American Medical Association for the seventh-grade reading level, potentially limiting patient comprehension.

links.outcome: Reading grade level of LLM education materials after instruction to target lower reading level, and accuracy
links.effect: Models reduced reading levels by 4.8 (ChatGPT), 6.9 (Gemini), 3.8 (Copilot) grade levels (P<.001) without compromising accuracy; seventh-grade target only reached by Gemini (7.9), others ~10-11.
links.quote: When instructed to revise patient education materials to improve understandability, all 3 large language models reduced reading levels by 4.8 grade levels (ChatGPT), 6.9 grade levels (Gemini), and 3.8 grade levels (Microsoft Copilot) ( P < .001) without compromising accuracy.

links.outcome: Accuracy and completeness of LLM materials generated for lower health literacy (seventh-grade) target
links.effect: Accuracy at seventh-grade level 4.60, 4.55, 4.20 vs unspecified 4.70, 4.85, 4.30; no significant differences in accuracy or completeness between reading level conditions.
links.quote: There were no significant differences in accuracy or completeness among the 3 large language models when comparing patient education materials generated at an unspecified reading level with those generated at the seventh-grade reading level.

links.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy and completeness of LLM answers to patient FAQs
links.effect: Mean accuracy 4.02, 4.16, 3.81 and completeness 4.07, 4.25, 3.62 (Likert 1-5); Copilot significantly less accurate and complete than ChatGPT and Gemini; experts noted some inaccuracies.
links.quote: Post hoc Dunn testing showed that responses generated by both ChatGPT and Google Gemini were significantly more accurate than those generated by Microsoft Copilot.

unlisted_practices: Prompting LLMs to rewrite patient education materials at a lower reading level

links.outcome: Accuracy of LLM patient education answers
links.effect: FAQ accuracy scores were 4.02 ± 0.7, 4.16 ± 0.7, and 3.81 ± 0.8; panelists also noted inaccuracies and omissions.
links.quote: Mean accuracy scores (Likert scale, 1–5) for responses generated by ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot were 4.02 ± 0.7, 4.16 ± 0.7, and 3.81 ± 0.8, respectively, corresponding to an accuracy level between “accurate” and “very accurate” for responses by ChatGPT and Google Gemini and between “moderately accurate” and “accurate” for Microsoft Copilot responses.

links.outcome: Requested lower reading level for patient materials
links.effect: Seventh-grade prompt reduced levels by 4.8/6.9/3.8 grades (P < .001); final means were 10.3 ± 1.0, 7.9 ± 0.8, 10.8 ± 1.6.
links.quote: When instructed to revise patient education materials to improve understandability, all 3 large language models reduced reading levels by 4.8 grade levels (ChatGPT), 6.9 grade levels (Gemini), and 3.8 grade levels (Microsoft Copilot) ( P < .001) without compromising accuracy.

links.outcome: composite readability grade level of LLM FAQ responses
links.effect: ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot generated FAQ responses at mean grade levels of 15.3 ± 1.4, 15.7 ± 1.9, and 14.6 ± 1.3, respectively (P = .002)
links.quote: Responses to patients’ frequently asked questions generated by ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot were written at mean grade levels of 15.3 ± 1.4, 15.7 ± 1.9, and 14.6 ± 1.3, respectively ( F = 6.67, P = .002).

unlisted_practices: Prompting large language models to generate patient education materials at a specified grade level (e.g., seventh-grade reading level) to improve readability

screen.practice: reading-level constraint via prompting for patient education materials
screen.reason: The study empirically tests whether prompting LLMs to target specific lower reading levels successfully lowers readability scores without degrading clinical accuracy/completeness.
